title: OS command execution via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} sink {sink} launches processes. Untrusted input in the command becomes command injection. This lexical rule flags the sink; the reviewer confirms arguments are trusted or passed as vectors via {safe}.
remediation: Use {safe} with separate arguments, never interpolated command strings.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed maintenance commands are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} executes external commands. Shell metacharacters in untrusted input break out of the intended command. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: {lang} codebases launching processes; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Command execution on untrusted input; HIGH severity.
why: {sink} launches {lang} processes from strings, so untrusted input becomes command injection.
fix: Allowlist commands where a shell is unavoidable.
Re-run the scan and confirm no sink remains on untrusted input.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.
